directions.description: Train SASRec with multiple negatives and generalized BCE to address negative-sampling overconfidence. Primary sources: [gSASRec paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07192), [official PyTorch implementation](https://github.com/asash/gSASRec-pytorch). This is a training-only change suitable for the first trial; improvement on this benchmark remains unverified.
directions.implementation:
Keep the supplied SASRec encoder and tied scoring embeddings initially. Sample K training negatives per nonpadding target, excluding the user's training interactions; start K=64, t=0.75, then consider K=256 if throughput permits. Compute embeddings only for valid target positions and chunk negative scoring to bound GPU memory. Replace BCE with:

import torch.nn.functional as F

def gbce(pos_logits, neg_logits, itemnum, t=0.75):
    # pos_logits: [N]; neg_logits: [N,K]; padding already removed
    k = neg_logits.shape[-1]
    alpha = k / max(itemnum - 1, 1)
    beta = 1.0 - t + alpha * t
    return (beta * F.softplus(-pos_logits.float())
            + F.softplus(neg_logits.float()).sum(-1)).mean() / (k + 1)

Use LR=1e-3 initially and allow sufficient validation patience for slower gBCE convergence. Prediction remains raw dot-product ranking, so retain the existing predictor writer and checkpoint architecture.

Shared requirements for all four trials: set DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; retain all four named categories and dataset routing; use existing preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42; honor SASREC_EPOCHS with default 200. Read only provided train/validation splits. Keep every artifact under the trial directory and use one GPU per trial. Select checkpoints using validation HR@10 and compare the four-category macro-average. Preserve the pinned evaluation protocol and use an isolated validation RNG so evaluation does not reset training randomness. Save the first evaluated checkpoint even when HR@10=0. Count all training and debugging against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget.

directions.description: Replace one-negative BCE with normalized sampled-softmax ranking. Meta's primary implementation provides a concrete SASRec configuration with sampled softmax and normalized embeddings: [configuration](https://github.com/meta-recsys/generative-recommenders/blob/main/configs/ml-3b/sasrec-sampled-softmax-n96-seqlen500-final.gin), [loss implementation](https://github.com/meta-recsys/generative-recommenders/blob/main/generative_recommenders/research/modeling/sequential/autoregressive_losses.py).
directions.implementation:
Retain SASRec, replacing its loss with this sampled candidate cross-entropy adaptation:

import torch.nn.functional as F

def sampled_ce(features, positive_emb, negative_emb, temperature=0.1):
    # shapes: [N,D], [N,D], [N,K,D]; valid positions only
    h = F.normalize(features.float(), dim=-1)
    p = F.normalize(positive_emb.float(), dim=-1)
    n = F.normalize(negative_emb.float(), dim=-1)
    positive = (h * p).sum(-1, keepdim=True)
    negative = torch.einsum('nd,nkd->nk', h, n)
    logits = torch.cat([positive, negative], -1) / temperature
    labels = torch.zeros(h.shape[0], dtype=torch.long, device=h.device)
    return F.cross_entropy(logits, labels)

Start K=128 uniformly sampled training negatives, excluding the user's training interactions, dropout=0.2, hidden dimension=64 and temperature=0.1. Consider temperature=0.05 and hidden dimension=128 only after the initial comparison. These are proposed local settings, not a reproduction of Meta's full experiment. Chunk valid positions when necessary.

Update SASRec.predict to normalize both final features and candidate embeddings before their dot product; apply the saved temperature consistently. Save normalization and temperature in metadata, and update write_predict_script to pass these constructor options when loading each dataset model. Apply the shared data, seed, routing, validation and budget requirements from direction 1.

directions.description: Add DuoRec-style contrastive regularization to SASRec to improve sequence representation diversity. Primary sources: [DuoRec paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.05730), [author implementation](https://github.com/RuihongQiu/DuoRec/blob/master/recbole/model/sequential_recommender/duorec.py).
directions.implementation:
Begin with the supplied SASRec BCE objective plus a dropout-view contrastive auxiliary loss. Two training-mode encoder passes over the same prefix produce views a and b; use their final nonpadding features. An economical symmetric cross-view adaptation is:

import torch.nn.functional as F

def dropout_nce(a, b, target, tau=0.2):
    a = F.normalize(a.float(), dim=-1)
    b = F.normalize(b.float(), dim=-1)
    logits = a @ b.T / tau
    eye = torch.eye(len(target), dtype=torch.bool, device=target.device)
    false_negative = target[:, None].eq(target[None, :]) & ~eye
    logits = logits.masked_fill(false_negative, float('-inf'))
    labels = torch.arange(len(target), device=target.device)
    return 0.5 * (F.cross_entropy(logits, labels)
                  + F.cross_entropy(logits.T, labels))

Set loss = recommendation_loss + 0.1 * dropout_nce(a,b,target). Start tau=0.2 and auxiliary weight=0.1; consider weights 0.05 or 0.2 after validation. For this auxiliary task, target is the next training item after the prefix, never a validation label. Reuse the first encoder pass for recommendation loss. A subsequent DuoRec extension can draw a different training prefix with the same next-item target as a semantic positive, indexed exclusively from training interactions.

This initial variant changes training only. Retain the existing SASRec predictor writer and disable dropout through eval() at inference. Apply the shared requirements from direction 1; account for the extra encoder pass when allocating trial runtime.

directions.description: Test FMLP-Rec as a distinct sequence encoder using learned frequency filters. Primary sources: [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.13556), [reference modules](https://github.com/RUCAIBox/FMLP-Rec/blob/master/modules.py), [reference model](https://github.com/RUCAIBox/FMLP-Rec/blob/master/models.py).
directions.implementation:
Replace attention blocks with frequency-filter residual blocks followed by feed-forward blocks. The core filtering operation is:

class FrequencyFilter(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, maxlen, hidden, dropout):
        super().__init__()
        self.weight = nn.Parameter(
            0.02 * torch.randn(1, maxlen // 2 + 1, hidden, 2))
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
        self.norm = nn.LayerNorm(hidden, eps=1e-8)

    def forward(self, x):
        spectrum = torch.fft.rfft(x.float(), dim=1, norm='ortho')
        weight = torch.view_as_complex(self.weight.contiguous())
        filtered = torch.fft.irfft(
            spectrum * weight, n=x.shape[1], dim=1, norm='ortho')
        return self.norm(x + self.dropout(filtered.to(x.dtype)))

Use item/position embeddings, two filter-plus-FFN blocks, hidden dimension=64, maxlen=128, dropout=0.3 and LR=1e-3 initially. Train on random training prefixes: choose cutoff c in [1,len(history)-1], input history[:c], target history[c], and score only the final position. Frequency mixing is noncausal, so the baseline's simultaneous shifted targets would expose earlier targets through later input positions. Prefix sampling prevents that leakage. Start with the baseline BCE loss to isolate the encoder change.

Keep model classes in train.py. Update write_predict_script to import the new class, instantiate it from saved architecture metadata, load its state dict, and score candidates from its final prefix representation. Preserve all four models and dataset_name routing. Apply the shared requirements from direction 1.
